observations: Two identical photos show a used black exhaust component lying on dirt ground.
The part is a catalytic converter integrated with an exhaust manifold, with flanges on both ends.
A watermark reading 'VICTOR EXHAUST SYSTEM' appears across the center of both photos.
No Hyundai logo, part number, or '2014' marking is visible on the part in either photo.
The seller's text claims it is for a Hyundai Elantra 2014 model.

identity.kind: used catalytic converter with exhaust manifold

claims.evidence: photo 0 and photo 1 show a catalytic converter assembly
no vehicle-specific markings or part numbers visible in the photos

risks.risk: The converter may not fit a Hyundai Elantra 2014 despite the seller's claim.
risks.proof: A clear close-up of any stamped part number on the metal, or a photo showing the part installed on the vehicle.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic used converter with unconfirmed fitment

risks.risk: The catalyst internals may be clogged, melted, or hollowed out.
risks.proof: A video or photo looking into both ends showing the honeycomb intact, or a cut-open view.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a dead or hollowed converter

risks.risk: The part may be cracked or damaged on sides not visible in the still photos.
risks.proof: A video rotating the part to show all sides and welds.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of any stamped part number or casting number on the converter body.
Video showing both open ends of the converter to confirm the honeycomb is intact.
Video rotating the part to reveal cracks or damage on all sides.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a used catalytic converter assembly from the photos, so it can be priced at its worst case even though the Hyundai Elantra 2014 fitment claim cannot be verified remotely.
